challenges.title: No Midwest state has data after a statewide law
challenges.text: Under current law the model expects Wisconsin to permit 0.07 per 1,000 single-family homes per year in 2027–2031 (645 permits ÷ 1,839.569 thousand homes ÷ 5 years); there is no observed statewide ADU series. States with before-and-after data (California, Rhode Island, Washington, Vermont) reached similar first-year levels however low they started, but they are coastal or New England markets. Iowa's first full year (2026) will be the first Midwest test.

challenges.title: Madison-like cities ran at a little over half the central scenario's rate in years 1–3
challenges.text: Medians of 0.45, 0.54 and 0.60 permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year in 9 Washington and Oregon cities, against the central scenario's statewide 0.77, 0.95 and 0.99. Only Madison is moved onto that path, so Madison's with-law rate sits below its suburbs'. If Wisconsin's other mid-size markets behave like those cities, the central is too high in its first three years; if Madison behaves like the statewide model, Madison is too low. Gate 5 will review this.

challenges.title: The hold-out test rests on 7 states
challenges.text: California in the common level wins in 66% of resamples of the 7 states, which is within noise. The lower and upper scenarios rest on how 8 states differ, one of them California.
